text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cooking gas cylinder blast blamed for fire near Mecca killing at least 217 Muslim pilgrims and injures 1,290.
- Singapore Haj pilgrims not affected by fire.
- Malayan Railway conducting inquiry into allegations it assigned Singapore businessman to collect rent from squatters.
- Englishwoman wins her share of Singapore $72 million estate from Court of Appeal.

- U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accuses Singaporean investor and unknown entity of illegal trading, using inside information related to Neptune Orient Lines (NOL) takeover bid for APL Ltd of U.S. to net more than Singapore $1.45 million in purchasing 1,690 APL call option contracts.
- NOL staves off criticism it is paying too much for APL and expresses confidence th takeover will boost NOL bottom line.
- Two more finance companies, Keppel and United Overseas introduce "innovative" car loan pack, joining Bank of America in offering new twists to attract business.
- Malaysian stock market recovers some poise after hitting nine-month low.
- Seventy-two locally authorised unit trusts qualify for 1997 Investment Fund Awards, jointly organised by Standard Chartered Bank and Business Times.
- MCL Land spending Singapore $1.1 billion on six new projects over next three years.
- Proposed new project by MCL Land expected to help even out its earnings over next few years.
- MMI Holdings shares, most hotly traded on Wednesday, earn only about four percent over its initial public offer price.
